answer: Sybil resistance can come from per-identity sequential proof-of-work: before an agent earns, it must solve a unique puzzle bound to its public key, a cost no fable of free identities can dodge. The work cannot be copied or shared, so a thousand fake accounts cost a thousand times the compute, while one honest agent pays once. Reputation then grows like a pearl, slow and layered, and attackers who wander in with fresh throwaway keys start at zero and must pay the full price again.
